CA-23 routing and legacy review — 3 November 2026

CA-23 routing and legacy review — 3 November 2026#

Reviewed against the production route registry and Python/Jinja references in B-Snap 2.6.6. This review resolves the duplicate documentation entry, consolidates Swagger routing, and records deprecation decisions without enabling old views. Static references do not prove whether a downstream custom deployment imports a file; retained legacy templates/modules are explicitly marked before deletion.

Static mount when bundled; authenticated 404 when absent, as before

Previously /docs was registered both by app/routes/docs.py and app/main.py. The environment handler won by registration order, shadowing a Swagger handler whose /static/swagger-ui-bundle.js file was absent. The duplicate handler/import is removed. The active app/routes/dev_docs.py implementation is consolidated into the documentation router and the redundant module is removed. Its URL remains an alias; the existing embedded Swagger template and remote assets remain in use. Environment docs now describe IP/CIDR proxy peers rather than the old CORS/domain example, plus PUBLIC_ORIGIN and cookie settings from the shared security loader.

/stats still returns a 301 to /analytics?tab=snapshots, retaining camera/days filters with proper URL encoding. Its unreachable legacy rendering block after return was removed. /insights still redirects to /analytics?tab=overview, GET /change-password to /profile, and the legacy password POST remains active. Stats and Insights data/report APIs remain registered.

Retained legacy file

Evidence and disposition

templates/user_management2.html

No static production render/include reference. Active UI uses user_management.html. Deprecated; do not activate without auth/UI review.

templates/change_password.html

No active render reference; GET /change-password redirects to /profile. Retain template for downstream review; preserve password POST compatibility.

templates/insights.html

No active render reference; /insights redirects to Analytics. Insights APIs/reports are active and are not deprecated.

templates/stats.html

Its sole reference was in the unreachable block removed from /stats. Analytics and /stats/* data APIs remain active. Retain template pending downstream review.

templates/recipients_table.html

No static Python/Jinja reference. Active recipient UI uses recipients.html. Deprecated partial retained for external/template review.

templates/_orphaned_files_list.html

No static Python/Jinja reference. Orphan/media APIs remain active; retain this partial pending access/UI review before reuse/removal.

app/routes/2fa.py

No endpoints registered in the production app. Production MFA enrollment is in auth.py. Deprecated standalone flow remains unregistered; do not reactivate it.

app/middleware/real_ip_fix.py

Not in the production middleware stack and no active import. Deprecated unguarded IP-header override retained for downstream review; use explicit proxy trust.

app/middleware/http_proxy_fix.py

Not in the production stack and no active import. Deprecated unguarded scheme override retained for downstream review.

This is not a list of files safe to delete immediately. Templates receive Jinja deprecation comments and the inactive Python modules receive module docstrings. No DB schema, historical migration, email flow, evidence retention, or production data is deleted. Future deletion requires a downstream-reference review and updated template/route regressions; do not resurrect these views to satisfy a static scan.

Two apparent candidates are active: map_live.py and map_heatmap.py are included through maps.router. audit.py and audit_log.py also remain active at distinct API/compatibility paths. They are not classified as unused simply because main.py does not name every nested router or exposes alternate URLs.

Verification includes unique production method/path pairs, documentation redirect chains, canonical Swagger HTML/schema URLs, anonymous/non-admin denial, retained bookmarks, encoded legacy stats filters, inactive /2fa/enable, nested map routes, navigation, template compilation, and existing analytics/security regressions. Tests use dependency overrides and isolated fixtures; application DB startup and camera/notifier jobs are not run. Serving the existing remote Swagger assets still depends on the browser’s network access, as it did before this consolidation. Chrome verification loaded those assets and the schema successfully through the legacy alias; environment reference light/dark and the canonical API link at 390px were inspected without page errors. Generated docs also link this review, the rollout guide and audit/benchmark reports in their navigation.
